quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

18 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Use alternate routes.
Drive the same way as on dry roads.
Stay farther behind other vehicles.
Avoid crossing bridges or intersections.

questions.explanation: On slippery roads, stay farther behind other vehicles. Your car will need more time to stop than it does on dry roads.

questions.question: When driving at highway speeds on a dry road, a safe following distance is at least:

options.text: Three seconds.
Two seconds.
Four seconds.
Two car lengths.

questions.explanation: On a dry highway, a four-second gap between you and the car ahead gives you enough time to steer or brake and avoid a hazard.

questions.question: The speed limit is ____ miles per hour when yellow lights are flashing on a school zone speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: When yellow lights flash on a school zone sign, or during school zone hours, you cannot drive faster than 15 mph.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow what the crossing guard tells you to do.
Do what other cars are doing, even if the crossing guard says something different.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal rules as if there were no children present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow what the crossing guard tells you to do.
questions.explanation: Always follow the directions given by a crossing guard, sign, or police officer in a school zone. Drive slowly and carefully in school zones.

questions.question: If a traffic light at an intersection is broken or not working, you should:

options.text: Stop and wait for it to be fixed.
Stop and wait for a police officer.
Treat it like a four-way stop.
Drive through normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection as a four-way stop.

questions.question: Taking drugs with alcohol:

options.text: Increases the risk of a crash.
Is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
Makes alcohol's effects weaker.
Does not affect your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs (prescription, over-the-counter, or illegal) can harm your brain function and make driving unsafe. Mixing alcohol with drugs greatly increases the chance of a crash.

questions.question: For a first conviction of driving under the influence of alcohol, you could:

options.text: Lose your license for up to five years.
Be required to take a class about drunk driving dangers.
Get a restricted license for work only.
Pay a fine of at least $300.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pay a fine of at least $300.
questions.explanation: A first offense for driving under the influence includes a fine between $300 and $5,000. The exact amount depends on your blood alcohol level.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Making you fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Emotions affect how well you drive. If you are worried, excited, afraid, angry, or sad, you may not drive well. Stress reduces your focus on driving. It is better to wait and drive when you feel calm.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway:

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
Pass only on the right.
Watch for oncoming traffic.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear and use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A left curve is ahead.
A series of curves is ahead.
An S-curve is ahead.
The road will be slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will be slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road becomes very slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle approaches you with its siren and/or flashing lights, you must immediately:

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights and sirens approaches, move to the right side of the road and stop.

questions.question: It is best to keep space around your vehicle:

options.text: Only in back of your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space on all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to danger. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left or right.

questions.question: What does this green arrow on a lane control signal mean?

options.text: You may use this lane.
No traffic is allowed in this lane.
You have the right of way.
You must merge into this lane.

questions.explanation: A green arrow pointing down over a lane means you can use that lane.

questions.question: You may turn left on a red light if:

options.text: There is no traffic coming from the opposite direction.
You are turning from a two-way street onto a one-way street.
You are turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street.
The car in front of you turns left.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street.
questions.explanation: You can turn left at a red light after stopping if you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street, unless a sign says you cannot. Always stop first and yield to pedestrians and other traffic.

questions.question: The "four-second rule" tells you how to:

options.text: Yield to other cars.
Turn at stop signs.
Follow another car.
Cross an intersection.

questions.explanation: On dry roads, keep at least four seconds of distance between your car and the car ahead of you.

questions.question: When driving where children are playing, you should expect them to:

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross the street.
Stop at the curb before crossing the street.
Run out in front of you without looking.
Not cross the street unless with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run out in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be extra careful around children. They may not understand danger and could run into the street without looking.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Continue normally through the intersection.
Stop and proceed when a green light appears.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means "caution." Slow down, look both ways, and move forward carefully.

questions.question: You can reduce the risk of hydroplaning by driving:

options.text: Through shallow water.
More quickly.
More slowly.
Through deep water.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slow down to reduce this risk.
